rules.title: auth
rules.why_flagged: function name or path is in the authentication surface
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Select the function also when it returns a boolean/int the caller uses in an if guarding a privileged operation. Attach every rule id that plausibly applies; the validator narrows. Also select when the function compares a credential, or when its result gates a login decision.

Also select when the function decides whether a principal may reach an object, or when the object's owner is never compared to the caller.

rules.title: secret handling
rules.why_flagged: secret is generated, stored or embedded here
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Also select for base64 blobs of 32 characters or more assigned to a key-like identifier - a length test the pattern does not make - and for PEM private key blocks anywhere in the tree.

rules.title: deserialization
rules.why_flagged: function turns bytes from outside into an in-memory object
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Also select a memcpy of a network buffer directly into a struct, which is the C spelling of the same bug and carries the alignment and padding problems with it.

rules.title: SPA/non-constant-time crypto
rules.why_flagged: cryptographic operation whose timing or power trace may depend on a secret
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Select the function also when it returns a boolean/int the caller uses in an if guarding a privileged operation. Attach every rule id that plausibly applies; the validator narrows. Also select when the function performs modular exponentiation, scalar multiplication, table lookups indexed by secret bytes, or branches on secret bits - none of which the pattern can see.

rules.title: non-constant-time comparison
rules.why_flagged: secret compared with an early-exit comparison
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Select the function also when it returns a boolean/int the caller uses in an if guarding a privileged operation. Attach every rule id that plausibly applies; the validator narrows. LOG-008 asks whether REMOTE timing is measurable; HW-009 is the same defect under a physical attacker. The scout emits both either way.

rules.title: session/token
rules.why_flagged: session or token is issued, stored, renewed or expired here
rules.flag_condition: Section 2.5 is explicit that these are not reliably grep-able: the candidate set is built by FUNCTION SELECTION and whole functions are handed to the validator, which is why match_target is function_or_path. Select the function also when it returns a boolean/int the caller uses in an if guarding a privileged operation. Attach every rule id that plausibly applies; the validator narrows. CWE: carry CWE-384 when the candidate is about fixation and CWE-613 when it is about expiry, or both where you cannot tell - but never CWE-384 by default: a cache with no lifetime tagged CWE-384 reads as a login-flow bug and gets dismissed as one. CWE-613 is the record default for that reason.

rules.why_flagged: function validates, or is named as if it validates, untrusted input

Also select the parsers: parse* over a message, packet, record, frame, header, hello, extension or blob, whether or not the name says validate.

rules.title: triage-rated logic pass
rules.why_flagged: the triage model rated this function high and no rule matched in it: a whole-function logic pass, not a matched sink
rules.flag_condition: Derived by stage 3, never grepped. The function performs an operation a caller should not reach unchecked, and no rule pattern names it. State the invariant (M1), name the protected operation at its line, and answer four absent-control questions in gates_evaluated, one object each: LOG-001 (is the caller authenticated before it, on every path), LOG-002 (may this caller act on this object), LOG-004 (is the origin of the input verified where the protocol needs it: a webhook signature or MAC, an update signature, a callback token), LOG-009 (is a one-time value, a nonce, a replay window or a session state checked). A missing control is a contract 8a claim (3) finding and owes a relevance_test. A function with no protected operation in it closes on FP-NOT-SECURITY with all four answers n/a, each citing a range that covers function_range. The triage verdict that raised this candidate is a model's reading of the function and is never evidence; the record carries none of it.
rules.derivation: Not grep-driven and not stage 1's: stage 1 never runs it and coverage.json has no row for it. Stage 3 (enrich_candidates.py) gives exactly one LOG-TRI candidate to each function the operating point selected whose stage-2 score record carries triage_verdict "high" (llm-triage only), that has no emitted rule hit, and that rules_lib.triage_derivation does not exclude (a <module> or <window> record, stage 1's test tree, a generated file, a directory segment third_party, vendor or node_modules), unless stage 2 ran with --no-triage-candidates (operating-point.json triage_candidates.enabled false) or left it out under --triage-candidates-max (the first N owed functions by rank are kept). line is the function's first line with text; sink_text is that line read off disk. Stage 2 counts these candidates into every CORPUS SHAPE row before the cut is chosen. The candidate gate recomputes the set from extract/, scores/ and operating-point.json (invariant I8) and accounts for it in candidates/coverage-selection.json triage_derived, not in the per-rule rows of coverage.json.
